danger_sign: Vaginal bleeding during pregnancy
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate urgent transfer and clinical evaluation at the nearest hospital or comprehensive emergency obstetric care facility. Do not insert anything vaginally.

danger_sign: Severe postpartum haemorrhage (PPH)
recommendation_paraphrase: Emergency medical treatment immediately. Call emergency transport or rush to the nearest emergency health facility for uterine massage, oxytocics, and resuscitation.

danger_sign: Convulsions / Fits / Loss of consciousness
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate emergency transfer to hospital. Clear airway, place on her left side, protect from injury, and administer magnesium sulphate as per protocol.

source_page_or_section: Module 4, Hypertensive Disorders in Pregnancy, p. 35-40
danger_sign: Severe persistent headache with blurred vision
recommendation_paraphrase: Urgent hospital evaluation to assess blood pressure, check proteinuria, and initiate anti-hypertensive and anticonvulsant prophylaxis.

danger_sign: Severe pain beneath the ribs / epigastric pain
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate hospital admission and urgent obstetric workup.

danger_sign: Decreased, weak, or absent baby movement
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate presentation at maternity centre for fetal heart auscultation and cardiotocography/ultrasound.

danger_sign: Acute shortness of breath or severe chest pain
recommendation_paraphrase: Emergency hospital admission with high-flow oxygen support and urgent medical evaluation.

danger_sign: Severe, persistent abdominal pain or rigid belly
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate emergency facility transfer for surgical and obstetric evaluation.

danger_sign: High fever, chills, and foul-smelling vaginal discharge
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate medical attention for IV broad-spectrum antibiotics and sepsis evaluation.

danger_sign: Thoughts of self-harm, suicide, or hurting the baby
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate crisis intervention. Ensure woman and baby are not left alone; escort to nearest hospital or mental health specialist immediately.

danger_sign: Waters breaking with foul smell or greenish/brown meconium stain
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate hospital transfer. Do not insert fingers or tampons; pad dry and present to labor ward.

danger_sign: Umbilical cord protruding from vagina
recommendation_paraphrase: Extreme surgical emergency. Call for an ambulance immediately. Mother should assume knee-chest position or elevate hips. Do not push cord back inside. Urgent hospital delivery.

danger_sign: Labour lasting over 12-24 hours without progress / severe maternal exhaustion
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate transfer to comprehensive emergency obstetric facility with surgical theatre capabilities for assisted delivery or Caesarean section.

danger_sign: Inability to suckle, latch, or feed at all
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate hospital evaluation for underlying severe systemic infection, hypothermia, or hypoglycemia.

danger_sign: Newborn convulsions, twitching, or stiff body spasms
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate hospital admission for airway management, anticonvulsant therapy, and infection workup.

danger_sign: Severe respiratory distress / Fast breathing (>=60 bpm) / Severe chest indrawing
recommendation_paraphrase: Emergency hospital presentation. Keep infant warm; urgent oxygen and antibiotic therapy required.

danger_sign: Severe hypothermia (<36.5C) or high fever (>37.5C)
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate medical assessment. If hypothermic, practice immediate skin-to-skin warming en route to facility.

danger_sign: Extreme lethargy, floppiness, or unresponsiveness
recommendation_paraphrase: Extreme emergency resuscitation and urgent hospital transport.

danger_sign: Severe jaundice (yellow skin extending to palms and soles, or appearing on Day 1)
recommendation_paraphrase: Immediate hospital evaluation for phototherapy or exchange blood transfusion to prevent permanent brain damage.

danger_sign: Red, swollen cord stump discharging pus or foul odour spreading to abdominal skin
recommendation_paraphrase: Urgent medical treatment with parenteral antibiotics to prevent rapid systemic bacteremia and peritonitis.

danger_sign: Severe continuous vomiting and inability to keep fluids down >24h
recommendation_paraphrase: Prompt clinic/hospital attendance for IV rehydration, electrolyte balance, and antiemetic therapy.

danger_sign: Painful burning urination with flank pain or fever
recommendation_paraphrase: Visit primary health centre within 24 hours for urine microscopy, culture, and pregnancy-safe antibiotics.

danger_sign: Tender, hard, hot, red breast wedge accompanied by flu-like fever
recommendation_paraphrase: Same-day clinic evaluation for antibiotic therapy, continue gentle frequent breast drainage, warm compress.

danger_sign: Mild bilateral ankle swelling without headache or facial puffiness
recommendation_paraphrase: Rest with feet elevated, maintain hydration, monitor for danger signs, and mention at next routine antenatal visit for blood pressure check.
